rationale: hammernik_2017-claude-agentic: vn_T=3, vn_n_filters=16, vn_kernel=9, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=2.0, vn_filter_init_std=0.05, vn_rbf_init_std=0.01, vn_lambda_init=0.02, epochs=30, batch_size=2, lr=0.00096, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=400, val_n=200, seed=42, max_train_s=1100, rationale=iter-3 (six-box). PREV NUMBERS: iter-1 hr=0.5777 (train_n=400, 30 full epochs, ~1084s) BEST; iter-2 hr=0.0947 REGRESSED (train_n=1600 same 1000s wall -> epochs wall-truncated ~7-8, fewer effective passes/sample -> under-trained; SSIM 0.9849->0.9567, RMSE 2.2e-3->4.7e-3). FAILURE MODE (iter-2): under-training from the wall cap, NOT data-hunger -- my iter-2 data-limited hypothesis is FALSIFIED (train_n change was confounded by reduced effective epochs). LESSON: this VN needs its full epoch budget to converge; keep train_n at the working 400 where 30 epochs FIT the budget. RESET baseline to the iter-1 WINNER. ONE KNOB vs iter-1: vn_lambda_init 0.0097 -> 0.02 (~2x stronger data-fidelity anchor to the FBP init). HYPOTHESIS: a stronger lambda anchor keeps each unrolled step closer to the clean FBP init and reduces the learned regularizer over-smoothing the recon, so val hr rises above 0.5777; predict hr > 0.59. All else = iter-1 (T=3, filters=16, kernel=9, n_bumps=31, x_range=2.0, epochs=30, lr=9.6e-4, batch=2, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, train_n=400). BUDGET: identical compute to iter-1 (lambda_init is free); max_train_s raised 1000->1100 so all 30 epochs complete (iter-1 hit 1084s and slightly clipped) -- still well under the 30-min SLURM kill. batch_size=2 (512px OOM guard).
